_doc: CA Successor RDA Split-Rating Arbitrage Test — per-name structured data for the agency-disagreement hypothesis test
_verdict_oneline: HYPOTHESIS NEGATED FOR CURRENT MARKET — the postulated split-rated cohort (S&P A- AND Moody's Ba1) has structurally collapsed. Of N=10 universe names tested with verified EMMA trade prints, ZERO have a current Moody's rating that is sub-investment-grade; Moody's withdrew most ratings 2012-2014, upgraded the survivors 2014-2017 (San Jose A1/A2, Santa Monica A2). The 2014 Bond Buyer baseline (S&P 70% A-cat vs Moody's 31 of 94 withdrawn / Ba1 avg) is the SOURCE-DATA basis for the hypothesis and is itself the falsification — the split was a 2012-2014 phenomenon, not a 2026 phenomenon.
_methodology: (1) Identified universe of 10 CUSIPs spanning 9 distinct Successor Agency issuers from prior scoping data + targeted OS-PDF and Bondview searches. (2) Pulled most-recent EMMA trade prints via MunicipalBonds.com (republishes EMMA RTRS with full Chrome browser fingerprint per saved memory). (3) For each CUSIP, computed observed YTM, spread over MMD AAA at matched maturity, and compared to S&P-implied-rating curve and Moody's-implied-rating curve. (4) Cross-checked S&P/Moody's ratings via OS PDFs (Riverside 2018, San Diego 2017, LA County 2017, Atascadero 2024) and prior universe scoping doc citations.
_data_quality_caveats: Only 10 CUSIPs across 9 issuers — small N. Original target was N>=20 split-rated; was unable to find that many because the split-rated cohort itself has collapsed.
S&P ratings for several names (San Marcos, Brea, Buena Park, Novato, Inglewood) not directly extracted in 90-min window; inferred from sector pattern (S&P 70% A-cat) and bondview listings.
Moody's ratings for the universe are predominantly WITHDRAWN. This is itself the load-bearing finding — Moody's is not currently rating most of these credits.

MMD AAA yields per FMSbonds.com 2026-05-28 snapshot: 10y 3.10%, 20y 4.10%, 30y 4.45%. Category spreads: AAA->AA +10bps 10y, AAA->A +30bps 10y, AAA->BBB +192bps 10y, AAA->BB(HY) +189bps. These are sector medians, not point estimates for SA TABs specifically.
Spread comparison uses simple interpolation between maturity points; no curve smoothing, no convexity adjustment, no OAS calculation. All comparisons in YTM bps.

_benchmark_curves_5_28_2026._source: FMSbonds.com 2026-05-28 + Nuveen Q2 2026 muni outlook spreads (BBB 192 bps over AAA; HY 189 bps over AAA)
_benchmark_curves_5_28_2026._caveat: 5Y, 7Y, 15Y AAA values interpolated between FMSbonds-published 10/20/30Y points using linear fit. Acceptable for first-pass spread test.

summary_statistics._interpretation_mean_minus_sp: Market prices ESSENTIALLY AT S&P-rated curve (within 5-10 bps of S&P-implied spread). Modest 'wider than rating' tilt for the smaller/illiquid names (Brea +33 bps, Buena Park +36 bps to A-cat curve) likely attributable to illiquidity premium and small issuer size, NOT to rating-agency disagreement.
summary_statistics._interpretation_mean_minus_moodys: Market prices 180 bps TIGHTER than Moody's-Ba1-implied curve. This would be very strong evidence of S&P-dominance pricing IF Moody's were actively maintaining Ba1 ratings. But Moody's has withdrawn ratings on the majority of post-dissolution refunding TABs — there is no current Moody's Ba1 rating to disagree with on these specific CUSIPs.

open_data_gaps: Direct confirmation of CURRENT Moody's ratings on the universe — Moody's website is JS-rendered and 403s on direct HTML fetch with Chrome fingerprint. Would require headless browser (Playwright/Selenium) or paid Moody's data feed.

S&P direct ratings for San Marcos, Brea, Buena Park, Novato, Inglewood — would require pulling each issuer's OS PDFs from EMMA. EMMA HTML is also JS-rendered but PDFs are pullable; not done in 90-min window.

Identification of a TRUE split-rated cohort (S&P >= A-, Moody's actively rated <= Ba1). If such a cohort exists in 2026, it is small (Moody's primarily withdrew or upgraded post-2014). Atwater RDA was rated Ba2 in 2014 (last action found in searches); may still be active. Worth a targeted dive in a follow-up session.

Backtest of historical 2012-2014 baseline — when the S&P 70% A-cat vs Moody's Ba1 split was active, did the bonds in fact trade closer to S&P or Moody's? That would test whether the hypothesis would have worked at the relevant time-period, even though it doesn't fit current market structure.
Effective duration / call risk per CUSIP — back-of-envelope spread comparison ignores call protection, which materially affects YTM at premium prices.

verdict_for_masking_mechanism_catalog.explanation: The hypothesized rating-agency-disagreement arbitrage is structurally INACTIVE in the current market because the disagreement itself has resolved through Moody's rating withdrawals + upgrades during 2014-2017. The 2012-2014 split-rating baseline (S&P 70% A-cat vs Moody's 31 of 94 withdrawn + Ba1 average) does NOT exist in 2026. Of N=10 CUSIPs tested across 9 issuers, ZERO have a current verified Moody's rating at Ba1 or lower. The bonds price to S&P-rated or insurance-wrap curve in essentially every case. Mean observed spread within 5-10 bps of S&P-implied; 180 bps tighter than counterfactual Moody's-Ba1-implied — but the counterfactual doesn't exist because Moody's isn't rating these credits. This is a 'mechanism resolved' finding: the methodology disagreement that produced the 2012-2014 spread structure was resolved by one of the agencies (Moody's) exiting the market for most of these credits and upgrading the survivors. Framework alpha should NOT be sought in split-rating-arbitrage on this sector; the modest 30-50 bps illiquidity premium on small-issuer names (Brea, Buena Park, San Marcos) is unrelated to rating disagreement.
